items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I like Rufus, particularly at that – I like Rufus for musical reasons, and also as a person. That’s how we did it. ... Not on my watch. You do not pay guys $400 a night. Way no. Not when we’re making this kind of money, and not Billy Hart, Cecil McBee, or Rufus”

ctx.x: I’m not talking about the screaming shit. I’m talking about boom boom. I said, “Nobody’s better equipped to do it than us, with Joe and with a first-class rhythm section.” I said, “Where Trane is the centerpiece. We owe it to him, and we’re the ones to do it.” The thing with Michael’s relationship with me was very – he absolutely respected me. It’s like, Randy was like a brother; Michael was like the younger brother. As to Randy, he was to me. Also because we were about three or four years apart too. Michael…

That was the genesis of that group. When he passed, the night he passed was IAJE, as you remember. Alice [Coltrane] had passed, very far out confluence. I was – we were all devastated. We played at 7 o’clock at night with my group, and then we all heard about it about 10 o’clock at night. At least I heard about it. Adam. Adam came. He found me. I remember, the first thing I do, I have to talk to Billy. I must talk to Billy, because Billy’s – he’s ahead of me, for sure. I said, I got to talk to somebody. I got to…

items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: people like myself, Dave Liebman and the other people who are part of this educational thing and have been for many years

ctx.x: Was it, I don’t know if “easier” is the right word, but for the Lester Youngs of the world, at that time, because jazz wasn’t codified into books and so forth, was it easier for him to be an individual? Nowadays there’s all the books to buy.

I think so. And yet I don’t know. He was different enough — I mean Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, they were different enough, but even the black community didn’t want to hear the stuff that they were coming up with because it was different than what they were doing or what they were used to, or it wasn’t part of the church, whatever. So I think anybody who really wants to go over here is looked kind of down on. And yet, that same mass of people who are not, if they stay individual long enough, then they…
Takes the life out of it.
